title: Chronos: tenant-aware throughput pinning and staged maintenance orchestrator
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: We need an orchestrator (Chronos) that automates node lifecycle and maintenance while preserving per-tenant throughput contracts. Chronos coordinates soft-cordon, staged draining, capacity-lease pinning for high-SLA tenants, autoscaler handshake for backfill waves, and KV preheat to avoid tail-latency regressions. Goal: perform upgrades and maintenance windows with minimal SLO perturbation and predictable billing/throughput guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Chronos can allocate a capacity lease for one or more tenant lanes and enforce throughput pinning during maintenance windows
Soft-cordon and staged drain complete within configured time windows without exceeding per-tenant tail latency thresholds (p95 and p99 SLOs) in synthetic and canary tests
Autoscaler integration can request temporary burst capacity and release it after backfill; no request is dropped as a result of maintenance for pinned tenants
KV preheat successfully restores >90% of warmed KV cache hit-rate for pinned tenants within first 30s after migration in lab tests
Rollback path exists: chronos aborts and returns leases within configured rollback window when error thresholds cross (errors or latency regressions)
Operational observability: per-tenant maintenance timeline and lease state visible in Console with trace links to node-level events
design_notes: Use explicit CapacityLease objects scoped to tenant IDs and throughput targets. Leases are soft tokens that block autoscaler from reassigning reserved slots until released.
Introduce a short-lived LeaseGrant API on the autoscaler to enable temporary burst capacity requests for backfill waves during maintenance
Maintain a 'staging' drain phase where KV preheat agents proactively transfer prefix caches to target hosts using asynchronous snapshot/restore rather than forcing cold starts
Prefer a multi-phase drain: soft-cordon -> connection-drain -> kv-prewarm -> gentle-eviction -> final-swap; make each phase timeboxed and observably abortable
Design Cron-like maintenance windows with tenant-aware priority queueing: critical tenants get earlier/isolated windows; lower-priority tenants can be compacted into opportunistic backfill waves
implementation_steps: Schema: add CapacityLease resource in control plane and RBAC rules for lease creation/inspection
Autoscaler: implement LeaseGrant endpoint and backfill admission check
Agent: extend node agent to support soft-cordon, KV snapshot/restore orchestration, and phase signals for Chronos
Controller: Chronos controller that orchestrates phases across host groups, enforces tenant lane constraints, and records timeline events for Console
Console: expose lease state, per-tenant maintenance timeline, and links to traces/PRs
E2E tests: synthetic traffic generator that can pin throughput to tenant lanes and assert SLOs during staged maintenance
risks: Incorrect lease accounting could starve best-effort tenants leading to customer complaints
KV preheat might amplify network/storage IO during backfill waves; need throttles to avoid cascades
Autoscaler handshake bugs could overprovision temporarily and increase cost without releasing leases
Edge cases during cross-region maintenance where global routing and local leases interact poorly
testing_plan: Unit tests for CapacityLease lifecycle and autoscaler LeaseGrant contract
Integration tests in a dedicated lab cluster simulating mixed tenant SLAs and verifying p95/p99 during maintenance
Chaos tests: inject node failures mid-drain and assert Chronos aborts and recovers leases safely
Canary rollout in staging with two high-SLA tenants and one low-priority tenant to validate metrics and Console UI
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal deployment to infra team for iterative feedback (1 week)
Beta: enable for a small set of customers under guidance of Solutions Eng (2 weeks)
GA: enable by default with opt-out for non-critical tenants; provide migration guide for customers with custom autoscaler integrations
